definition: BuddhaBot (Japanese: ブッダボット) is a chatbot trained on early Buddhist texts and designed to answers questions based on them.
details: The project has been developed by a group led by Seiji Kumagai and Toshikazu Furuya at Kyoto University.

explainer.lead: BuddhaBot is a chatbot designed to answer questions using early Buddhist texts rather than draw on every subject equally. It offers a focused way to explore those writings through conversation.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a librarian who has studied one special collection of old books and answers questions using that collection. BuddhaBot is like that librarian for early Buddhist texts: you ask a question, and it gives an answer based on those writings.
tiers.practitioner: BuddhaBot applies conversational question answering to a narrow textual domain: early Buddhist texts. A practical evaluation should check whether answers are supported by those texts and whether the system acknowledges questions outside its scope. Its specialized training should not be treated as a guarantee of accuracy, completeness, or religious authority.
tiers.paperLevel: BuddhaBot can be described as a learned mapping f(q) -> a, where q is a user question and a is an answer intended to be grounded in a corpus T of early Buddhist texts. Its defining limitation is domain specialization: performance and coverage depend on that corpus, and textual grounding alone does not establish interpretive or doctrinal authority.

explainer.example: A user could ask, “What do early Buddhist texts say about suffering?” BuddhaBot would then give a conversational answer based on its training on those texts, rather than attempting to represent every Buddhist tradition or later commentary.

usedIn.name: Early Buddhist text exploration
usedIn.detail: Provides conversational answers to questions based on early Buddhist writings.

usedIn.name: Domain-specific question answering
usedIn.detail: Illustrates how a chatbot can be specialized for a defined body of religious literature.

explainer.intuition: A general chatbot may answer questions about almost anything, while BuddhaBot is built around one particular body of knowledge. Its answers are meant to come from early Buddhist texts, making the subject area part of the system's design.
howItWorks: Early Buddhist texts provide the material on which the chatbot is trained.
A user asks BuddhaBot a question in a conversational interface.
The chatbot produces an answer based on those texts.
The development work is led by Seiji Kumagai and Toshikazu Furuya at Kyoto University.
explainer.whyItMatters: BuddhaBot shows how conversational AI can provide a focused entry point into a specialized collection of texts. Its value depends on answers remaining grounded in that collection and on users understanding its limited scope.
misconceptions: It is not a claim that the chatbot is the Buddha or possesses spiritual insight.
Training on early Buddhist texts does not make it an authority on every Buddhist tradition.
A text-based answer is not automatically accurate, complete, or the only valid interpretation.
